review_summary: Strong, complete plan: all 12 MEDIUMs from memory #610 plus D1/D2 are covered with no silent drops, waves are file-disjoint with the T6/T10 quality-runners boundary stated explicitly on both tasks, and the load-bearing premises I spot-verified (M2's unused isSidecarReachable at lifecycle.ts:80/162, unguarded stopSidecarProcess at :193, M6's if(store) gate at mcp-tools.ts:69, M10's session-end divergence at hook.ts:97-130) all check out against source. Two design-level should_fixes: the M10c 'dispatcher wins' rule would enshrine the dispatcher's session-end sidecar-stop without re-evaluating it against v1.36.2 H1's revised lifecycle, and M2b's 'unreachable → remove files' orphans a live-but-wedged sidecar — the exact class M4b fixes in runtime.

issues.title: M10c's blanket 'dispatcher wins' rule may enshrine a sidecar-stop that contradicts H1's revised lifecycle
issues.description: Verified: the dispatcher's runSessionEnd (src/cli/commands/hook.ts:97-130) calls stopSidecarProcess() in TWO code paths (lines 111 and 128), while the standalone src/hooks/session-end.ts never touches the sidecar at all — it only stops the dashboard when getActiveSessions() is empty and uses a direct MemoryStore. This divergence is bigger than the plan's 'sidecar-first vs direct-only' framing: it is 'stops the shared sidecar' vs 'doesn't'. v1.36.2's H1 fix was precisely about NOT killing the shared sidecar out from under other live consumers (OpenCode plugin sessions, other assistants, sessions the local store can't see). Pre-Mortem 2's resolution rule ('the dispatcher's behaviour wins — it ships') would carry the sidecar-stop into the extracted processSessionEnd unexamined, potentially reintroducing the H1 failure mode through the hook path. Note also: the standalone hook is NOT dead code to be steamrolled — the OpenCode plugin and any direct invocation路径 matter.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an explicit carve-out to Task 13/M10c: the session-end sidecar-stop divergence must be resolved against H1's post-v1.36.2 semantics, not by the blanket rule. Concretely: the extracted processSessionEnd may stop the sidecar only under the same guard discipline the H1 fix gave the MCP server (provably no other active consumers), or not at all — decide by reading src/mcp/server.ts's current cleanup and matching it. Require the task report to state which behaviour was chosen and why, and add a Truth asserting session-end does not kill a sidecar that other sessions are using.

issues.title: M2b's 'unreachable → remove files, do NOT signal' orphans a live wedged sidecar — the class M4b just fixed
issues.description: Verified against src/sidecar/lifecycle.ts: isSidecarReachable() returns false for 'process alive but not serving' (line 104-105 — probe failed on a live PID, e.g. a wedged or still-starting sidecar). Under M2b as written, stopSidecarProcess would then 'remove files, do NOT signal': cleanupSidecarFiles() unlinks the pid/socket/port files of a process that may be a real, live sentinal sidecar. That process is now orphaned forever — alive, holding DB handles and possibly a bound socket, with no record pointing at it and a fresh sidecar spawned beside it. Task 3's M4b codifies the opposite doctrine for runtime ('never delete a record while the group may live; keep the pidfile, return ok:false'). The plan cites 'the runtime domain's doctrine' as justification for not signalling, but applies only half of it — runtime keeps the record when it can't act safely; M2b deletes it. Also unflagged: the /health identity check makes stopSidecarProcess async, and it has sync callers at src/cli/commands/sidecar.ts:123,155 and hook.ts:111,128 that must be updated.
issues.suggested_fix: Amend Task 7/M2b: for an alive-but-unreachable PID, attempt an identity check that doesn't need HTTP — e.g. `ps -o command= -p <pid>` and match the sentinal sidecar argv (mirroring src/runtime/ownership.ts's approach; note the v1.36.2 `etime`-not-`etimes` portability lesson already in Gotcha 8). Identity confirmed → SIGTERM is safe; identity unverifiable → remove files without signalling BUT log the potential orphan loudly (pid + reason). Add a RED test: alive-but-not-serving sidecar is either terminated (identity match) or reported as a possible orphan — never silently forgotten. Also list the stopSidecarProcess sync→async ripple (sidecar.ts:123,155; hook.ts:111,128) in the task's files/steps.

issues.title: Task 10's Verify runs the FULL suite + build:opencode mid-Wave-2, contradicting Gotcha 5 and colliding with T6/T7's in-flight sidecar edits
issues.description: Task 10's Verify is `bun test src/ && bun run build:opencode`. In a shared-working-directory wave, that runs every test in the repo — including src/sidecar/ (where Task 6 is mid-edit on lsp-client.ts/quality-runners.ts and Task 7 on lifecycle/routes/server/client) and src/spec/ (Task 8) — while those agents are in flight. The plan's own Gotcha 5 says 'judge the full suite only at wave boundaries'; Task 10's verify command violates it and will report false failures from other agents' domains. build:opencode is worse: the plugin bundles from src/ (embed-assets), so the bundle bakes whatever half-finished sidecar state exists at that moment. Lesser instance: Tasks 6 and 7 both verify with `bun test src/sidecar/`, so each sees the other's in-flight state.
issues.suggested_fix: Narrow Task 10's Verify to its own files: `bun test src/sidecar/observation-queue.test.ts src/utils/file-log.test.ts src/memory/auto-decay.test.ts ...` (its touched-file tests), and move `bun run embed-assets && bun run build:opencode` plus the full-suite gate to the Wave 2 boundary (the orchestrator's wave check, where Truth 19 already lives). For T6/T7, either scope each to its owned test files or explicitly note in both tasks that cross-agent src/sidecar failures mid-wave are expected in-flight states (Gotcha 5 applies).

issues.title: Task 9's conditional mid-task split of mcp-tools.ts (582/600) is near-certain to trigger — pre-decide it
issues.description: Verified: memory_maintain registration is gated at src/memory/mcp-tools.ts:69 (`if (store) registerMaintainTool(server, store);`) and the file is 18 lines from the hard block. M6b requires: unconditional registration, a client-mode handler that opens a scoped MemoryStore per call, a documented 'why no sidecar route' note, and a DESTRUCTIVE description flag. That is realistically 15-30 net lines — the 'keep the change tiny' branch will almost certainly lose, and the task then does a pure-move split under TDD-guard friction mid-task (Gotcha 4) as an improvised step. Truth 19 ('every touched non-test file < 600') makes this a hard gate, so leaving it conditional just defers a known decision.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the split unconditional: either add it to Wave 1 (a tiny pure-move task alongside Task 1, same discipline: tests byte-unchanged) or make it the mandatory first mini-step of Task 9 rather than an 'if it cannot absorb' fallback. Precedent already named in the plan: spec/mcp-tools.ts split.

issues.title: M1d (byte framing) as a mid-task fallback is the right call structurally, but the deferral target is undefined
issues.description: Pre-Mortem 1 defers M1d if Task 6 balloons ('report, don't silently drop'). M1d cannot be pre-split into a parallel Wave 2 task — it edits the same lsp-client.ts/lsp-transport.ts files (wave file-disjointness forbids it). But the fallback as written leaves the deferred work homeless: no Wave 3 slot, no follow-up plan mention, and Truth 19 has no line-item for it, so 'report' can quietly become 'drop'. Note the split itself helps here: if Task 6 extracts framing/transport to lsp-transport.ts FIRST, M1d becomes a small isolated change to the new file and is less likely to be the thing that balloons.
issues.suggested_fix: Two small edits: (1) in Task 6, order the steps so the lsp-transport.ts extraction happens before M1d, making the framing fix a contained diff; (2) add to Pre-Mortem 1: 'if deferred, M1d becomes an explicit Wave 3 task (lsp-transport.ts only — file-disjoint from all Wave 3 tasks) and its Truth is marked deferred in the plan', so the fallback has a landing site instead of a report line.

issues.title: Four load-bearing premises not independently re-verified (audit-sourced, mostly un-re-verified by the orchestrator)
issues.description: Within review budget I verified M2 (lifecycle.ts read in full — isSidecarReachable exists at :80, autoStartSidecar uses kill(pid,0)-only isSidecarRunning at :162, stopSidecarProcess unguarded at :193), M6's if(store) gate (mcp-tools.ts:69), M10's session-end divergence (hook.ts:97-130 vs hooks/session-end.ts), and that lsp-client.ts does carry a `projectPath` field (:118, consistent with M1's re-root claim). NOT independently verified: (a) M1's exact re-init condition (`!isReady()`), the timeout-resolves-empty path, and the UTF-16-slice framing bug; (b) M7's deepMergeAdditive usage and wholesale permission-key deletion in uninstall; (c) M9's claim the MCP SDK accepts a full ZodObject and wraps raw shapes non-strict; (d) M11's plugin-side queue reader format. All four come from audit agents whose MEDIUMs were mostly not orchestrator-re-verified.
issues.suggested_fix: No plan change required — each affected task already mandates a RED test through the real entry point, which will falsify a wrong premise before implementation. Add one sentence to Tasks 6, 9(M9a via Task 4), 10, and 11: 'first step: confirm the audit premise against source; if it does not hold, stop and report rather than implementing against the plan's description.' (Task 4's M9a listTools/inputSchema assertion and Task 10's explicit plugin-reader check already do this in spirit.)
